observations.title: Deployment dates now reject impossible calendar days
observations.detail: Candidate compares parsed calendar components instead of relying only on Date.parse. Tests add impossible dates. No direct payment or manifest-signature bypass established.

observations.title: RPC transport explicitly suppresses browser ambient metadata
observations.detail: Candidate sets credentials omit, no-referrer, and no-store. Main does not set these options. Browser egress integration reviewer owns route reachability and wider deployment policy; this is not independently ranked here.

observations.title: Nonfinite retry counts are clamped to zero
observations.detail: Main Math.min/Math.max preserves NaN, making the retry termination comparison ineffective. Candidate guards Number.isFinite. No externally controlled browser path to the retry option was established.

observations.title: Bulk router evidence can avoid per-match followup reads
observations.detail: Candidate selects matched plus cover transactions and supports batch verification without live fallback for missing entries. Canceled batches discard partial evidence and stop new calls; dispatched RPCs keep the client timeout/retry policy. All requested include entries can exceed the nominal cover-selection cap by design. Integration privacy claims need the app-level batching and scan-disclosure context.

observations.title: Receipt evidence relies on configured providers and verified deployment inputs
observations.detail: Received status binds canonical block/receipt/transaction/calldata and exact announcement, plus payer-to-recipient Transfer for supported ERC20. Secondary evidence must agree when configured; provider independence and manifest authenticity are caller obligations. Registry/announcer presence and behavioral probes are documented as not runtime-code pins.

observations.title: Pre-sign review depends on independent expected intent and policy
observations.detail: Decoder uses closed selectors, canonical reencoding, exact typed-data fields, and rejects authorizationList. Reviewer binds policy and expected intent, with direct-sweep gas caps and allowance limits. Buffer router method is deliberately refused in tx-review though the adapter builder supports it. Policy/expected intent authenticity and immediately-before-sign use are caller duties.

observations.title: Chain adapter verification TODO trails current token/feed tables
observations.detail: TODO-VERIFY still describes two listed USDC entries and an empty FEEDS table, while runtime lists more sourced testnet tokens and four feed entries. External address/source correctness was not independently verified in this source-only batch.

followups.title: Aggregate work budget for secondary-provider comparison
followups.detail: compareProviders range-halves/regrows and accumulates secondary logs without a local aggregate request/log budget. Primary fetch defaults bound its own calls to 50 and accepted logs to 10000, not necessarily the secondary work over the same block range. A stricter or inconsistent secondary can cause substantially more work per primary page. No probe or operational amplification estimate was performed. scan_network_round2 independently reported candidate scopedClient wraps both providers, gates new dispatch before/after each request, and races abort; main lacks that wrapper. Candidate cancellation should therefore not be reported absent just because the package API has no AbortSignal. App reviewer retains main cancellation analysis and any final severity.
